slides.title: One configuration, every agent, a state you can go back to
slides.lede: aval describes the setup once and gives it to Claude Code and to Pi. Each version is kept, can be pinned and rolled back, and its cost is measured.
slides.note: The promise: the same rules everywhere, a known state, and real numbers about usage.

slides.title: A generation is a frozen copy of the setup
slides.lede: Everything aval writes for every agent, stored read-only under a name made from its content. Same content, same name.

slides.title: Today the setup only lives in place

items.title: Written twice
items.text: Claude Code and OpenCode get their config from separate code; nothing proves they say the same.

items.title: No way back
items.text: A sync overwrites. Going back to last Tuesday is not possible, only to the run just before.

items.title: No idea of cost
items.text: Usage windows run out without warning, and no one knows which project spent them.

items.title: One model
items.text: Rules, skills, commands, hooks, permissions and MCP described once.

items.title: Adapters
items.text: Claude Code and Pi read the model; what an agent cannot do is warned about, never dropped.

items.title: Generations
items.text: Build, activate, roll back and pin a frozen copy.

items.title: Usage
items.text: Tokens per project, session, day and consumer, checked against ccusage.

items.title: Pen boots
items.text: It starts Pi on generation 3f2a, pinned.

items.title: The owner changes a rule
items.text: aval sync builds generation 9c41 and activates it for Claude Code.

items.title: Pen is untouched
items.text: It keeps 3f2a until it is told to move.

items.title: aval usage --by consumer
items.text: Interactive, daemon and headless shares of the 5 h and 7 d windows.

slides.title: Rules that are tests, not promises

items.title: Projected or reported
items.text: Every part of the model is written or warned about.

items.title: One generation per run
items.text: A run never mixes two states.

items.title: Host settings win
items.text: The overlay can add a deny, never remove one.

items.title: No ambient config
items.text: Adapters read only what they are given.

items.title: Subscription billing
items.text: No API key is ever written or forwarded.

slides.title: From the repo to each agent

items.title: Loader
items.text: Reads the repo as it is today into one Config.

items.title: Adapter
items.text: Renders files for one agent and lists the losses.

items.title: Generation store
items.text: Keeps the rendered files by content hash.

items.title: Activator
items.text: Swaps one link, checks the doctor, restores on failure.

slides.title: Why it is built this way
rows: HCS-style ids and a content hash
The spec is a single-author draft that changes weekly
They already back up, verify and restore
Pi gets its own agent dir
No ambient config, nothing leaks from the user's Pi
On a subscription, dollars are not the limit
